svg.text: In-Depth Technical Flow of the 7 Key Security Classes • Spring Security 6 • Exception Handlers & OAuth Lifecycle
PART 1: REST API SECURITY EXCEPTION HANDLERS (401 UNAUTHORIZED & 403 FORBIDDEN)

g.text: • When it triggers: No JWT, expired token, or forged HMAC signature
• When it triggers: Employee accessing HR endpoint

svg.text: PART 2: GOOGLE OAUTH 2.0 AUTHENTICATION & USER LIFECYCLE (5 CLASSES)

g.text: • What it does: Exchanges authorization code for OpenID token and extracts Google claims: sub, email, name, picture
• Delegates to: Calls oAuth2AuthService.processOAuth2User(email, name, sub) to manage database state
• Method: public User processOAuth2User(String email, String name, String googleSub)
CASE 1: User Already Exists in DB
• Preserves existing role (HR, MANAGER, or EMPLOYEE)
• Saves new user entity via userRepository.save(newUser)
• Why it exists: Bridges Google's raw attributes with our internal PostgreSQL User entity
• Authorities Attached: Maps database role to Spring authority: List.of(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_" + user.getRole().name()))
• Provides Accessors: getId(), getEmail(), getName(), getEmployeeCode(), getRole()
• When it triggers: User cancelled Google prompt, or account is inactive / locked
• Redirects to: Browser login page with query param:
Next.js UI renders clean red alert banner
• When it triggers: Google authentication succeeded and user entity is ready
• Mints JWT Token: Calls jwtService.generate(user) with role authorities
• Redirects to: Next.js Client Bridge with token & user metadata in URL:
Next.js stores JWT in localStorage and forwards user to /employee, /manager, or /hr!
JWT saved to localStorage • Full Name & Code displayed in Shell Header
